inductive TmP : Type
  | lit  : Int -> TmP
  | tvar : Nat -> TmP
  | add  : TmP -> TmP -> TmP
  | mul  : TmP -> TmP -> TmP
  | powp : TmP -> TmP -> TmP

def evalTmP (env : Nat -> Int) : TmP -> Int
  | TmP.lit n    => n
  | TmP.tvar k   => env k
  | TmP.add a b  => evalTmP env a + evalTmP env b
  | TmP.mul a b  => evalTmP env a * evalTmP env b
  | TmP.powp a b => (evalTmP env a) ^ (evalTmP env b).toNat

def evalTmNP (env : Nat -> Nat) : TmP -> Nat
  | TmP.lit n    => n.toNat
  | TmP.tvar k   => env k
  | TmP.add a b  => evalTmNP env a + evalTmNP env b
  | TmP.mul a b  => evalTmNP env a * evalTmNP env b
  | TmP.powp a b => (evalTmNP env a) ^ (evalTmNP env b)

def substTmP (k : Nat) (t : TmP) : TmP -> TmP
  | TmP.lit n    => TmP.lit n
  | TmP.tvar j   => if j = k then t else TmP.tvar j
  | TmP.add a b  => TmP.add (substTmP k t a) (substTmP k t b)
  | TmP.mul a b  => TmP.mul (substTmP k t a) (substTmP k t b)
  | TmP.powp a b => TmP.powp (substTmP k t a) (substTmP k t b)

theorem evalTmP_powp (env : Nat -> Int) (a b : TmP) :
    evalTmP env (TmP.powp a b) = (evalTmP env a) ^ (evalTmP env b).toNat := rfl

theorem evalTmNP_powp (env : Nat -> Nat) (a b : TmP) :
    evalTmNP env (TmP.powp a b) = (evalTmNP env a) ^ (evalTmNP env b) := rfl

theorem substTmP_powp (k : Nat) (t a b : TmP) :
    substTmP k t (TmP.powp a b)
      = TmP.powp (substTmP k t a) (substTmP k t b) := rfl
authoring.origin: ROUND 2 for refusal-symbolic-exponent, carrying the PASSED p7-parallel-tower-r1 verbatim and adding EXACTLY ONE walker case the committed class measurement (tests/test_symbolic_exponent_class.py) still names as unmet.  r1 covered the `evalTm` and `substTm` cases (+ their rfl lemmas); the measurement lists the queue in order `evalTm, evalTmN, substTm, substTm_evalTm, check`, so the next unmet in list order is the `evalTmN` (Nat-valued) evaluator.  Added: `evalTmNP` mirroring the committed `evalTmN (env : Nat -> Nat) : Tm -> Nat`, plus its `powp` rfl lemma `evalTmNP_powp` -- where the exponent is already `Nat` so the symbolic power needs no `.toNat` coercion at all, the cleanest of the three walkers.  One addition per round keeps a regression attributable.  Still a PARALLEL tower appended after the committed slice (cannot extend `Tm`), still a PROPOSAL and never a slice edit.
